text: Corp. v. Admiral Ins. Co. (1995) 10 C4th 645, 688, 42 CR2d 324, 349] • [3:296] Liability for acts committed prior to the policy period is covered under a claims-made policy unless the policy contains either: — a “prior acts exclusion”; or — a “retroactive date” (excluding coverage for injury suffered before a certain date even if first claimed during the policy period). [3:296.1 - 3:296.4] Reserved. (c) [3:296.5] Compare—“claims made and reported” coverage: Some CGL policies may require that the claim also be reported to the insurer during the policy period (so-called “claims made and reported coverage”). Cross-refer: Claims-made and claims made and reported coverage are discussed in detail in Croskey, Heeseman, Ehrlich & Klee, Cal. Prac. Guide: Insurance Litigation (TRG), Ch. 7A. (2) [3:297] “Personal injury liability” coverage: A separate provision, “Personal and Advertising Injury Liability Coverage,” covers the insured's liability for damages because of specified offenses (¶ 3:298) committed in the course of the insured's business activities.
